evidence.red_check: Flipped the runtime instead of the code: copied the shipped /app/classes/com/guided/orci/OrciApplication.class out of the app container and launched it on a Java 21 JVM (docker run eclipse-temurin:21-jre-jammy java -cp /c com.guided.orci.OrciApplication). It went red with 'java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError: com/guided/orci/OrciApplication has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 69.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 65.0'. The same class on the app container's Java 25 JVM loads (fails later only with NoClassDefFoundError org/slf4j/LoggerFactory because no libs were on the classpath, i.e. version check passed). Nothing was changed in the app container, so no revert was needed. IMPORTANT: this red check ran in a throwaway sibling container, not inside the app under test, so the signature below does NOT appear in the captured application log. There is no app-level condition to flip for a build/toolchain ticket; a pre-fix class swap would only recompile the same sources at a lower target and is not the behaviour the ticket is about. That is why the verdict is inconclusive rather than deploy-ready.

CI Build runs the unit suite via mvnw install; the -P integration-tests profile is not part of CI, so 'full test suite on Java 25' means the CI suite. It was not re-run locally here.

automation.assessment: Toolchain pins are already enforced structurally (setup-java 25 in every workflow, java.version property in every pom, jib base image following the property), and CI/CD on JDK 25 is the real regression net. Nothing rule- or UI-level to lock in. One cheap guard is worth considering against the stale-bytecode drift seen in the loop image.
proposed_tests: qa-suite @core smoke (SMOKE family): GET /actuator/info (or a small admin endpoint exposing Runtime.version()) asserts the running JVM feature version is >= 25, so a rollback of the jib base image or a stale image fails the post-deploy run.

Backend build-time check (surefire in orci module): assert every class in the orci-utils / orci-models jars on the test classpath has class-file major version == the configured java.version, catching a module that silently compiles at a lower target.

jira_comment:
Verdict: inconclusive.

Positive: The main build runs on Temurin 25.0.4.1, all shipped classes are Java 25 bytecode, the app boots healthy and login plus an authenticated API call succeed.
Negative: No pom or workflow still pins Java 21, and no Java-related errors appear in the boot log.
Red check: The shipped main class launched on a Java 21 JVM fails with UnsupportedClassVersionError (class file version 69.0), but this ran outside the app container so it is not an app-log red check.

CI Build and PR Gate are green on the PR head and dev deploys on main have passed on Java 25 since 2026-09-17, which covers the ticket's done criteria from GitHub rather than from this instance.
The MGB OpenShift check could not be performed from this environment.
